pharm: A non-systemic combination antacid (hydroxymagnesium aluminate) that dissociates in gastric acid into magnesium hydroxide and aluminium hydroxide, neutralizing gastric hydrochloric acid, raising intragastric pH, and reducing pepsin activity.
quick: 400-800 mg between meals and at bedtime (suspension 5-10 mL)
Take about 20-60 minutes after meals and at bedtime
Short-term standard-dose use acceptable; avoid prolonged/high dosing
Low milk transfer; not expected to harm the infant; use cautiously
No specific adjustment; avoid in hepatic coma with renal failure risk
No direct interaction; alcohol worsens acid symptoms
Serum magnesium/phosphate, renal function with prolonged use
summary: Magaldrate is an over-the-counter combination antacid consisting of a chemically defined hydroxymagnesium aluminate complex. On contact with gastric acid it converts rapidly to magnesium hydroxide and aluminium hydroxide, which neutralize gastric hydrochloric acid, raise intragastric pH, reduce hydrogen-ion back-diffusion, and lower pepsin activity. The magnesium component gives quick onset while the aluminium component provides prolonged buffering and a protective mucosal layer, and each component's gastrointestinal effect (magnesium laxative, aluminium constipating) partly offsets the other. It is used short-term for dyspepsia, heartburn, hyperacidity, and symptomatic relief of GERD, and off-label for peptic ulcer and esophagitis. It acts locally and is largely non-absorbed, although small amounts of aluminium and magnesium are absorbed and can accumulate in renal impairment, which is the key safety concern. Magaldrate is NOT FDA-approved as a single-ingredient agent in the modern openFDA database and has been discontinued as a standalone product in the US market (formerly Riopan).
indications: Symptomatic relief of gastroesophageal reflux / hyperacidity
Adjunctive symptom relief in gastric and duodenal ulcer and reflux esophagitis (older/off-label use)

dosage.d: 400 mg three to four times daily (max 3200 mg/24 h)

dosage.n: Risk of aluminium and magnesium accumulation

admin: Chew tablets thoroughly; shake the suspension well before use
Take about 20-60 minutes after meals and at bedtime for the longest acid-neutralizing effect
Separate from other oral medicines by 1-2 hours (at least 4 hours for levothyroxine and fluoroquinolones)
Do not self-treat for more than 2 weeks without medical advice
moa: Magaldrate is a distinct hydroxymagnesium aluminate complex that, on reaching the stomach, is rapidly converted by gastric hydrochloric acid and dissociates into magnesium hydroxide and aluminium hydroxide. These neutralize gastric acid, raise intragastric pH, and decrease the free hydrogen ion available for mucosal back-diffusion. Magnesium hydroxide reacts quickly for rapid onset, while aluminium hydroxide releases hydroxide slowly for prolonged buffering and forms a protective mucosal coating. The raised pH reduces the proteolytic activity of pepsin; magaldrate may also bind bile acids and has reported cytoprotective effects. Because the hydroxides are poorly absorbed, its action is essentially local and non-systemic, with the unabsorbed complex eliminated in the faeces.

absolute: Significant or severe renal impairment / renal failure
relative: Hepatic coma with risk of renal failure
monitor: Serum magnesium and phosphate with prolonged or high-dose use
Serum aluminium and renal function in renal impairment

preg: Generally regarded as acceptable for short-term symptomatic use at standard doses; chronic or high-dose use should be avoided, and some references advise avoiding the first trimester. It is not established as definitively safe or harmful in pregnancy.
lact: Milk excretion is low and harm to the infant is not expected; use cautiously and avoid prolonged high doses.
renal: Avoid or use with great caution in significant renal impairment. Impaired clearance can lead to hypermagnesemia, aluminium toxicity, osteomalacia and bone pain, and dialysis encephalopathy; chronic use also risks hypophosphatemia.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is required, but avoid in hepatic coma where there is a risk of concomitant renal failure and magnesium accumulation.

major: Reduces the efficacy/absorption of integrase inhibitors (dolutegravir, raltegravir) and pazopanib
May cause systemic alkalosis with sodium polystyrene sulfonate
moderate: Decreases absorption of tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, iron salts, digoxin, levothyroxine, oral antidiabetics, indomethacin, and benzodiazepines by binding or by raising gastric pH
minor: Generally alters the absorption rate of many oral drugs - separate dosing
interactions.food: Take after meals; no major specific food interaction.
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; alcohol can worsen acid-related symptoms.
interactions.diagnostics: Chronic use can alter serum phosphate, magnesium, and aluminium; may affect gastric-pH-dependent tests.

emergency: Signs of hypermagnesemia (severe drowsiness, slow or weak heartbeat, low blood pressure, muscle weakness, respiratory depression)

monitoring: Serum aluminium and renal function (chronic use or renal impairment)
counsel: Use only short-term (no more than about 2 weeks) without seeing a clinician
Chew tablets well or shake the suspension before use; take after meals and at bedtime
Space other medicines by 1-2 hours (at least 4 hours for thyroid medicine and certain antibiotics)
Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease or are on a low-magnesium diet
You may notice constipation or loose stools
Report persistent abdominal pain, black or bloody stools, or symptoms lasting more than 2 weeks
pk: Local luminal effect - no systemic plasma peak
About 20-60 minutes fasting, up to ~2-3 hours when taken after a meal
Store at room temperature, away from moisture and heat; keep suspension tightly closed
pearls: NOT FDA-approved as a single-ingredient agent (discontinued in the US; formerly Riopan) - use OTC/BNF monographs
The balanced aluminium-magnesium combination offsets the diarrhea of magnesium against the constipation of aluminium
Often combined with simethicone (and sometimes oxetacaine) in current OTC products in India and Bangladesh
The key safety pearl is to avoid use in renal impairment because of aluminium and magnesium accumulation
Separate from fluoroquinolones, tetracyclines, iron, and levothyroxine to avoid reduced absorption
missed: This is an as-needed antacid. Take it when you remember if you still need it; if it is near the next dose, skip it. Do not take a double dose and do not exceed the maximum daily amount.
overdose: Overdose can cause hypermagnesemia (weakness, hypotension, bradycardia, CNS and respiratory depression), aluminium accumulation, hypophosphatemia, milk-alkali syndrome, and severe diarrhea or constipation. Management is supportive with hydration and correction of electrolytes; dialysis may be needed in renal failure, and cardiac or neurologic symptoms require emergency care.
